$comment: Schema matches orca-dispatch config/roster.default.json: a policy block plus a roles map of { model, fallback }. The conversion from the old flat { primary, fallback } shape dropped anthropic:claude-sonnet-5 from both builder chains: orca-dispatch's dispatch.ts refuses the claude harness today (orca-dispatch #16), so that level was declared but never executable - a fallback level that silently does nothing. It comes back when #16 lands.
_note: Model refs are 'provider:id'; the id may contain colons and slashes, so refs split on the FIRST colon only. 'fallback' is a comma-separated chain tried left to right - the dispatcher splits it, and one attempt per level is all it gets. Harness is derived from the provider, never stored: anthropic -> Claude Code, codex -> codex, agy -> Antigravity, everything else -> pi. Note 'openai-codex' is not 'codex' and derives to pi.
_note_openrouter: Free-tier account, no credits. A paid OpenRouter id passes auth and then dies at request time with a 402. ':free' ids are not reliable either: z-ai/glm-5.2:free returns 429 from the shared upstream pool under load (orca-dispatch findings #13). Check a free id live before trusting it as a fallback.
_note_selfreview: No model reviews its own work. With the builder on ZAI, review must come from openai-codex or anthropic - never from zai or an OpenRouter ZAI id. The reviewer chain is gpt-5.5 then claude-opus-5 (orca-dispatch #10, findings #56); the fallback is declared here so it is a chosen reviewer, and a review that ran on it says so.
